literal: Emperor Shizong Wenxiang, taboo name Cheng, style Zihui, was the eldest son of Shenwu; his mother was Empress Dowager Lou.
idiomatic: Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong of Northern Qi, bore the personal name Cheng and the style Zihui. He was the eldest son of Gao Huan; his mother was Empress Dowager Lou.

literal: From birth he was precocious and sharp; Shenwu regarded him as extraordinary.
idiomatic: From birth he was precocious and keen; Gao Huan took him for a prodigy.

literal: In the first year of Zhongxing of Wei he was established as heir of the Prince of Bohai.
idiomatic: In Zhongxing 1 (531) he was made heir to the Prince of Bohai.

literal: He went to Du Xun to study; his quick comprehension surpassed others, and Xun greatly admired him.
idiomatic: He studied under Du Xun; his quickness of mind surpassed all others, and Du Xun came to admire him deeply.

literal: In the second year he was given Palace Attendant, Grand Lord Equal to Three Imperator, and married the Princess Chang of Fengyi, sister of Emperor Xiaojing; he was then twelve, with a handsome and spirited bearing, already like a grown man.
idiomatic: In the second year he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Lord Equal to Three Imperator and married Princess Chang of Fengyi, Emperor Xiaojing's sister. He was twelve, handsome and spirited, already bearing himself like a man.

literal: Shenwu tested him on the gains and losses of current affairs; his analysis never missed the mark, and from then on he took part in every military and state plan.
idiomatic: Gao Huan tested him on the affairs of the day; his analysis never missed the mark, and from then on he was included in every plan of war and state.

literal: In the first year of Tianping he was given Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Inspector of Bing Province.
idiomatic: In Tianping 1 (534) he received Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and the inspectorship of Bing Province.

literal: In the third year he entered to assist court governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.
idiomatic: In the third year he entered the capital to assist in governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and made Grand Commander of the Capital Region.

literal: Though people had heard of his talent and judgment, they still looked on him as a youth; yet his strategy was strict and clear, affairs never stalled, and court and countryside were stirred to solemn order.
idiomatic: Though men had heard of his talent, they still treated him as a youth; yet his plans were strict and clear, nothing hung fire, and court and countryside alike were stirred to order.

literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he acted as Minister of Personnel.
idiomatic: In Yuanxiang 1 (538) he served as acting Minister of Personnel.

literal: In Wei, since Cui Liang's time.
idiomatic: In Northern Wei, since the time of Cui Liang,

literal: appointments had been governed by years of service; Wenxiang then reformed the former practice, and selection and promotion rested only on getting the right men.
idiomatic: appointments had been governed by seniority; Gao Cheng reformed the old practice so that selection rested only on finding the right men.

literal: He also sifted the clerks of the Masters of Writing and finely chose men of talent and standing to fill the posts.
idiomatic: He also sifted the clerks of the Masters of Writing and chose men of talent and standing to fill the posts.

literal: As for men of talent and name, all were recommended and promoted; even those not yet in high office he brought into his household as retainers. Whenever he toured gardens and hills he always summoned them; they shot arrows, composed verse, and each displayed his strength — all for pleasure.
idiomatic: Men of talent and reputation he recommended and promoted; those not yet in high office he took into his household as retainers. Whenever he toured gardens and hills he summoned them; they shot arrows, composed verse, and each showed his gift — all for pleasure.

literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was given Grand General, Director of the Secretariat Supervisor, and still acted as Minister of Personnel.
idiomatic: In Xinghe 2 (540) he was made Grand General and Director of the Secretariat Supervisor while still serving as acting Minister of Personnel.

literal: From after Zhenguang the realm had been in turmoil, and among officials in office few were honest.
idiomatic: Since the Zhenguang era the realm had been in turmoil, and among officials in office few were honest.

literal: Wenxiang then memorialized to make Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful and wealthy without sparing any, and custom was renewed — private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.

literal: He posted notices in the streets setting forth the arts of governing the state, and opened a path for blunt speech; those who submitted memorials or letters with bitter and penetrating words he all received with favor.
idiomatic: He posted notices in the streets setting forth the arts of governing the state and opened a path for blunt speech; those who submitted memorials or letters with bitter and penetrating words he all received with favor.

literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Wuding, Shenwu campaigned west and, falling ill, withdrew the army; Wenxiang raced to the army's camp, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Wuding 4 (546), Gao Huan marched west, fell ill, and withdrew; Gao Cheng raced to the army, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.

literal: In the first month of the fifth year, on bingwu, Shenwu died; the death was kept secret.
idiomatic: In the first month of Wuding 5 (547), on bingwu day, Gao Huan died; the death was kept secret.

literal: On xinhai, Minister of Works Hou Jing held Henan in rebellion, and Sima Shiyun, Inspector of Ying Province, opened the city to him.
idiomatic: On xinhai day Minister of Works Hou Jing rebelled and held Henan, and Ying Inspector Sima Shiyun opened the city to him.

literal: Jing lured and seized Yuzhou Inspector Gao Yuancheng, Xiangzhou Inspector Li Mi, Guangzhou Inspector Bao Xian, and others.
idiomatic: Hou Jing lured and seized Yuzhou Inspector Gao Yuancheng, Xiangzhou Inspector Li Mi, Guangzhou Inspector Bao Xian, and others.

literal: He sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.

literal: In the fourth month, on renshen, Wenxiang attended court at Ye.
idiomatic: In the fourth month, on renshen day, Gao Cheng attended court at Ye.

literal: In the sixth month, on jisi, Han Gui and the others withdrew the army from Ying Province.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi day, Han Gui and the others withdrew from Ying Province.

literal: On dingchou Wenxiang returned to Jinyang, then announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Shenwu's final wishes.
idiomatic: On dingchou day Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang, announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Gao Huan's final wishes.

literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu, the Wei Emperor edicted that Wenxiang be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.
idiomatic: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the Eastern Wei emperor edicted that Gao Cheng be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.

literal: Wenxiang memorialized to decline the post and wished to relinquish the princely rank.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng memorialized to decline and wished to relinquish the princely rank.

literal: On renyin the Wei Emperor edicted that Duke of Taiyuan Yang administer military and state affairs, and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.
idiomatic: On renyin day the emperor edicted that Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang administer military and state affairs and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.

literal: In the eighth month, on wuchen, Wenxiang memorialized to carry out Shenwu's final command, asking to reduce the fiefs of the realm and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuchen day, Gao Cheng memorialized to carry out Gao Huan's final command, asking to reduce the royal fief and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.

literal: On xinwei he attended court at Ye and firmly declined the chancellorship.
idiomatic: On xinwei day he attended court at Ye and firmly declined the chancellorship.

literal: The Wei Emperor edicted: "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your original wish; there must be a taking of authority by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."
idiomatic: The emperor edicted, "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your wish; authority must be taken by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."

literal: Discussants all said Hou Jing still had a mind to look north, but only the command had not reached him.
idiomatic: Those who debated the matter all said Hou Jing still looked northward, but only the command had not reached him.

literal: Again Jing's officer Cai Zundao returned north and said Jing had a mind to repent.
idiomatic: Again Hou Jing's officer Cai Zundao returned north and said Hou Jing wished to repent.

literal: The Prince believed it true and thought he could be lured back; he sent Jing a letter saying:
idiomatic: Gao Cheng believed it and thought he could be lured back; he sent Hou Jing a letter saying,

literal: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you — you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.
idiomatic: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you—you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.

literal: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel — how much more when the bond was weightier than this?
idiomatic: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel—how much more when the bond was weightier than this?

literal: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.
idiomatic: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.

literal: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.
idiomatic: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.

literal: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.
idiomatic: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.

literal: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house — with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.
idiomatic: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house—with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.

literal: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.
idiomatic: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.

literal: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.
idiomatic: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.

literal: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.
idiomatic: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.

literal: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.
idiomatic: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.

literal: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment — yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.
idiomatic: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment—yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.

literal: I meant to seize the moment, sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.
idiomatic: I meant to seize the moment and sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.

literal: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.
idiomatic: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.

literal: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.
idiomatic: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.

literal: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.
idiomatic: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.

literal: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others — open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.
idiomatic: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others—open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.

literal: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.
idiomatic: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.

literal: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.
idiomatic: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.

literal: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand — if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.
idiomatic: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand—if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.

literal: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.
idiomatic: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.

literal: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back — we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.
idiomatic: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back—we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.

literal: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.
idiomatic: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.

literal: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong — in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.
idiomatic: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong—in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.

literal: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot — can you be without shame!
idiomatic: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot—can you be without shame!

literal: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say: "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent" — I do not know whether these words are empty or real.
idiomatic: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say, "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent"—I do not know whether these words are empty or real.

literal: The logic of fortune and calamity — I think you will weigh it yourself.
idiomatic: The logic of fortune and calamity—I think you will weigh it yourself.

literal: Jing replied in a letter:
idiomatic: Hou Jing replied in a letter:

literal: I, a humble man of the village lanes, by nature unfit for arts and use, entered service for the state and have passed two decades, braving peril and treading hardship without shunning wind and frost — thus I gained wealth in those years and glory in this life.
idiomatic: I, a humble man of the village lanes, by nature unfit for arts and use, entered service for the state and have passed two decades, braving peril and treading hardship without shunning wind and frost—thus I gained wealth in those years and glory in this life.

literal: Why did I once raise the banner and beat the drum and face north in resistance?
idiomatic: Why did I once raise the banner and beat the drum and face north in resistance?

literal: Truly because I feared peril and death and dreaded drawing calamity.
idiomatic: Truly because I feared peril and death and dreaded drawing calamity.

literal: In the late months of the year before, the honored king fell ill; the spirits did not bless the good, and prayers brought no cure.
idiomatic: In the late months of the year before, the honored king fell ill; the spirits did not bless the good, and prayers brought no cure.

literal: Thus favorites played with power, trusted hearts were divided, and though wife and children were at home they were besieged without cause.
idiomatic: Thus favorites played with power, trusted hearts were divided, and though wife and children were at home they were besieged without cause.

literal: When I returned to Changshe and hoped to state my case, the summons had not yet been sent and the axe was already at hand.
idiomatic: When I returned to Changshe and hoped to state my case, the summons had not yet been sent and the axe was already at hand.

literal: Though banners faced each other and we were not a bowshot apart, I sent letters again and again, hoping to make my humble feeling plain.
idiomatic: Though banners faced each other and we were not a bowshot apart, I sent letters again and again, hoping to make my humble feeling plain.

literal: Yet the commanders relied on their strength and looked down on me; battle followed battle, thrust on thrust, and they sought only to slaughter and destroy.
idiomatic: Yet the commanders relied on their strength and looked down on me; battle followed battle, thrust on thrust, and they sought only to slaughter and destroy.

literal: They dug ditches and dammed water until only three boards of wall remained; we looked at each other, lives hanging by the dripping clepsydra.
idiomatic: They dug ditches and dammed water until only three boards of wall remained; we looked at each other, lives hanging by the dripping clepsydra.

literal: Unable to bear death, I went out to fight below the wall and was seized and sent to Qin — would I do that for pleasure?
idiomatic: Unable to bear death, I went out to fight below the wall and was seized and sent to Qin—would I do that for pleasure?

literal: Beasts hate death; human relations love life — I am truly guiltless; what crime had Huan and Zhuang?
idiomatic: Beasts hate death; human relations love life—I am truly guiltless; what crime had Huan and Zhuang?

literal: Moreover the honored king in former days treated me as an equal; we strove together with one heart and jointly upheld the imperial house — though power was unequal and cold and heat differed slightly, Chancellor and Minister of Works were only like geese in flight.
idiomatic: Moreover the honored king in former days treated me as an equal; we strove together with one heart and jointly upheld the imperial house—though power was unequal and cold and heat differed slightly, Chancellor and Minister of Works were only like geese in flight.

literal: Fortune, salary, office, and glory are heaven's rank; granted after labor — reason does not connect with seeking to swallow charcoal; how absurd!
idiomatic: Fortune, salary, office, and glory are heaven's rank; granted after labor—reason does not connect with seeking to swallow charcoal; how absurd!

literal: Yet to steal another's goods is still called theft.
idiomatic: Yet to steal another's goods is still called theft.

literal: Salary taken from the public house — can one say it was not taken?
idiomatic: Salary taken from the public house—can one say it was not taken?

literal: Now Wei's virtue though declined, heaven's mandate is not yet changed; to receive favor in a private residence — what need to speak of it?
idiomatic: Now Wei's virtue though declined, heaven's mandate is not yet changed; to receive favor in a private residence—what need to speak of it?

literal: You mock me for being unable to seal Hangu Pass in the east and for being controlled by others — it is as if you praised Jizhong and commended the Ji clan.
idiomatic: You mock me for being unable to seal Hangu Pass in the east and for being controlled by others—it is as if you praised Jizhong and commended the Ji clan.

literal: A realm without a lord — in ritual I have not heard of it; to act without law — with what will you instruct?
idiomatic: A realm without a lord—in ritual I have not heard of it; to act without law—with what will you instruct?

literal: I hold that dividing wealth to nurture the young is a matter of proper ending; leaving a house to preserve the orphan — who would call that a petty grudge?
idiomatic: I hold that dividing wealth to nurture the young is a matter of proper ending; leaving a house to preserve the orphan—who would call that a petty grudge?

literal: Again you say my host is not enough to strengthen myself and my person is in peril like a pile of eggs.
idiomatic: Again you say my host is not enough to strengthen myself and my person is in peril like a pile of eggs.

literal: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, the ten rebels of Zhou fell; Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs — the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.
idiomatic: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, the ten rebels of Zhou fell; Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs—the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.

literal: Weight and light depend on the man, not the tripod on virtue; if one can be loyal and faithful, though weak one must become strong; deep sorrow opens the sage, and dwelling in peril — what hardship is there?
idiomatic: Weight and light depend on the man, not the tripod on virtue; if one can be loyal and faithful, though weak one must become strong; deep sorrow opens the sage, and dwelling in peril—what hardship is there?

literal: Moreover now Liang's way is harmonious and bright; it gathers men by ritual, covers them with tiger-pattern robes, and ties them with noble ranks — it intends to park the five peaks as a garden and pool the four seas, sweep foul vapors and save the black-haired people.
idiomatic: Moreover now Liang's way is harmonious and bright; it gathers men by ritual, covers them with tiger-pattern robes, and ties them with noble ranks—it intends to park the five peaks as a garden and pool the four seas, sweep foul vapors and save the black-haired people.

literal: East it bridles Ou and Yue; west it opens the road to Qian and Long; Wu and Yue are fierce and strong, girded with armor in thousands; Qin troops and Ji horses, bows drawn in tens of thousands — one blast of great wind and dry trunks must break; frost gathers for a moment and autumn girdles fall of themselves — if this is called weak, who is fit to be called strong?
idiomatic: East it bridles Ou and Yue; west it opens the road to Qian and Long; Wu and Yue are fierce and strong, girded with armor in thousands; Qin troops and Ji horses, bows drawn in tens of thousands—one blast of great wind and dry trunks must break; frost gathers for a moment and autumn girdles fall of themselves—if this is called weak, who is fit to be called strong?

literal: Again I see slander of wavering between two sides and suspicion from two states — weighing human feeling, how excessively!
idiomatic: Again I see slander of wavering between two sides and suspicion from two states—weighing human feeling, how excessively!

literal: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.
idiomatic: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.

literal: Dark and bright depend on the lord; use and discard depend on the man — follow ritual in action, and the spirits will reject evil!
idiomatic: Dark and bright depend on the lord; use and discard depend on the man—follow ritual in action, and the spirits will reject evil!

literal: Your letter speaks of sharp soldiers and horses and fixing a day for joint advance, exaggerating the situation and surely wishing mutual destruction.
idiomatic: Your letter speaks of sharp soldiers and horses and fixing a day for joint advance, exaggerating the situation and surely wishing mutual destruction.

literal: Truly cold glue and white dew — the season is the same; wind raises dust and the horses' heads — what difference is there?
idiomatic: Truly cold glue and white dew—the season is the same; wind raises dust and the horses' heads—what difference is there?

literal: You know only the north's struggle for strength and do not see the southwest's alliance — if you wish to follow your whim on the road ahead, you do not notice the pitfall at your side.
idiomatic: You know only the north's struggle for strength and do not see the southwest's alliance—if you wish to follow your whim on the road ahead, you do not notice the pitfall at your side.

literal: Leave peril for safety — now return to the orthodox calendar;
idiomatic: Leave peril for safety—now return to the orthodox calendar;

literal: turn calamity into blessing — already escaped the net.
idiomatic: turn calamity into blessing—already escaped the net.

literal: They will mock my past confusion; this too laughs at your obscurity.
idiomatic: They will mock my past confusion; this too laughs at your obscurity.

literal: Now I lead two states, raise banners and march north to attack; bears and tigers strive together, recover the central plains — Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the Guanxi; Xiangcheng and Xianhu already submit to the Jiangnan — take them yourself; what need to ask aid?
idiomatic: Now I lead two states, raise banners and march north to attack; bears and tigers strive together, recover the central plains—Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the Guanxi; Xiangcheng and Xianhu already submit to the Jiangnan—take them yourself; what need to ask aid?

literal: Yet expedients are not one; reason has ten thousand paths. For your plan, nothing surpasses ceding land and making peace in two parts, three shares standing like the tripod — Yan, Wei, Zhao, and Jin enough for salary; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all return to Great Liang.
idiomatic: Yet expedients are not one; reason has ten thousand paths. For your plan, nothing surpasses ceding land and making peace in two parts, three shares standing like the tripod—Yan, Wei, Zhao, and Jin enough for salary; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all return to Great Liang.

literal: Let me lend strength to the southern court, north I honor kinship by marriage; silks go of themselves, war chariots need not be driven — I stand and achieve merit for the age, you finish your fathers' and grandfathers' enterprise; each keeps his frontier, each enjoys the seasons; the hundred surnames are at peace, the four classes dwell secure.
idiomatic: Let me lend strength to the southern court, north I honor kinship by marriage; silks go of themselves, war chariots need not be driven—I stand and achieve merit for the age, you finish your fathers' and grandfathers' enterprise; each keeps his frontier, each enjoys the seasons; the hundred surnames are at peace, the four classes dwell secure.

literal: How does that compare with driving farmers from the fields, facing fierce enemies on three sides, avoiding weapons at head and tail, and meeting blades and arrows at the heart?
idiomatic: How does that compare with driving farmers from the fields, facing fierce enemies on three sides, avoiding weapons at head and tail, and meeting blades and arrows at the heart?

literal: Even if the Grand Duke were general, he could not survive; return to the high and bright — how could success be achieved?
idiomatic: Even if the Grand Duke were general, he could not survive; return to the high and bright—how could success be achieved?
